ops.issue: 暑い means uncomfortably/very hot (weather). 'ameno / agradavelmente quente' (mild / pleasantly warm) is the meaning of 暖かい, not 暑い. The en gloss ('hot (of weather)') and the pt natural translation ('mais quente') are correct; this gloss teaches the wrong word sense.

before.jp: 一年の中で夏が一番暑い
before.kana: いちねんのなかでなつがいちばんあつい

structure_explanation.en: Here the superlative 〜のなかで〜がいちばん〜 appears, 'among X, Y is the most 〜'. 一年の中で ('within the year') is the compared set, marked by 〜のなかで; 夏が points out the winning item with が; 一番暑い ('the hottest') joins the adverb 一番 to the い-adjective 暑い. Note that 暑い is 'hot' when speaking of weather/ambient temperature.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Aqui aparece o superlativo 〜のなかで〜がいちばん〜, 'dentre X, Y é o mais 〜'. 一年の中で ('dentro do ano') é o conjunto comparado, marcado por 〜のなかで; 夏が aponta o item vencedor com が; 一番暑い ('o mais quente') junta o advérbio 一番 ao い-adjetivo 暑い. Repare que 暑い é 'quente' falando de clima/temperatura ambiente.

before.jp: 時間もないしお金もない

structure_explanation.en: The sentence lists two problems with the particle 〜し (the target), each in the negative form ない (there isn't/I don't have). 時間もない (don't have time either) is followed by 〜し, which adds another reason, and then お金もない (don't have money either). The two も reinforce the accumulation: 'neither time nor money.'

Os dois も reforçam o acúmulo: 'nem tempo, nem dinheiro'.
